title: Descent of a chain comparison through natural K-injective representative models
statement: Let B and A be abelian categories with unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and suppose B has K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let U:B→A be exact additive and preserve K-injective complexes. Let HB and HA be bifunctors on cochain complexes, and DB and DA bifunctors on their derived categories. Suppose each has specified representative isomorphisms DB(QK,QI)≅Q HB(K,I) and DA(QK,QI)≅Q HA(K,I), for arbitrary K and K-injective I, natural in both complex variables. Given a natural chain isomorphism HB followed by termwise U ≅ HA after termwise U in both variables, there exists a natural isomorphism DB followed by D(U) ≅ DA after D(U) in both variables. On every pair of K-injectives its comparison, followed by the two canonical D(U) localization factors and the target representative map, equals D(U) of the source representative map followed by the localization factor on HB and Q of the given chain comparison.

source.place: Sections 0A8X and 08J7, Lemma 0A95; componentwise and localization assembly from steps 4–5 of lem-sf-ringed-forget-two-injective-hom.

proof.text: Restrict both complex variables to the full category of K-injective complexes. Its localization functor L=ι⋙Q is a localization at quasi-isomorphisms; the opposite product P=Lᵒᵖ×L is also a localization. These are the existing KInjectives and localization APIs, using the K-injective comparison of homotopy classes.

The source representative maps form a natural isomorphism eB over P. The target representative maps evaluated on U of the two K-injective complexes similarly form eA, since U preserves K-injectives. Combine eB, the localization factor for U, the given chain isomorphism, inverse eA, and inverse factors in both variables to obtain an isomorphism P⋙(DB⋙D(U)) ≅ P⋙((D(U)ᵒᵖ×D(U))⋙DA).

Precomposition by a localization is fully faithful on functor categories. Take the preimage of the preceding natural isomorphism. The map-preimage identity gives its value on every pair of K-injectives. Cancel the inverse target representative isomorphism and the inverse two-variable factor to obtain precisely the asserted representative equation.

proof_origin.place: Formal categorical assembly of the product-total Hom and K-injective models in Sections 0A8X and 08J7.

lean.statement:
theorem kInjectiveHomComparisonDescent :
    ∃ derived : DB ⋙ U.mapDerivedCategory ≅
        (U.mapDerivedCategory.op.prod U.mapDerivedCategory) ⋙ DA,
      ∀ (K I : CochainComplex B ℤ) [K.IsKInjective] [I.IsKInjective],
        derived.hom.app (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K), DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) ≫
            DA.map
              (X := (op (U.mapDerivedCategory.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)),
                U.mapDerivedCategory.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)))
              (Y := (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)),
                DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I)))
              ((U.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app K).op,
                U.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app I) ≫
            (ρA ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)
              ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I)).hom =
          U.mapDerivedCategory.map (ρB K I).hom ≫
            U.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app (HB.obj (op K, I)) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map (chain.hom.app (op K, I))
